title: IPAS: bank details and the changed-account flag
changes: IPAS: Purchasing types the supplier's Bank Name, Account Name and Account # in section 3. Finance, Super Admins and the section 1 and 3 approvers can read them; Finance can't change them, and a section 7 Noted or Checked signer without those roles reads the IPAS but not the bank details.
IPAS: an Account # that differs from the same supplier's most recent IPAS is flagged beside the account. Spaces and dashes don't count as a difference, and a supplier's first IPAS is never flagged.
IPAS: a flagged account clears the approvals given on sections 1 and 3 and notifies whoever prepared them. History records that the bank details changed, never the account number itself.

title: IPAS: payments, charges and Landed Cost
changes: IPAS: Purchasing and Finance record any number of payments (down payment, payment, full payment, shipping fee) and importation charges. Each has its date and amount, a payment its charge fee, method, Check No. and optional proof of payment. Edit or remove them until the IPAS is filed; every change is kept in History.

IPAS: on a foreign-currency PO each payment records the PHP actually debited, so costs use the rate really paid. DP and FP come from the payment rows, P.I/QT Amount is typed, and no balance is worked out.
IPAS: each IPAS gets one freight service and a computation status: Encoding, Encoded, Costs complete, Checked by.

IPAS: Landed Cost shows per line and per unit, spread by value, by quantity or equally, marked provisional until Costs complete and final after. A foreign PO with no payment shows it as not available.
IPAS settings: Purchasing and Super Admins edit the payment method, charge kind and freight service lists. Options are reordered or deactivated, never deleted, and rows that used one keep it.

title: IPAS: the Odoo copy stays current, with overrides
changes: IPAS: opening an IPAS refreshes it from Odoo and notes what changed since the last copy: lines added or removed, and new quantities or prices. When Odoo doesn't answer, the last copy shows with its fetch time.

IPAS: Purchasing can override Entity, Source Doc. and Analytic Dist., with Odoo's value shown beside the override and one click to go back to it. Currency, Supplier, item lines and Brand stay as Odoo has them.
IPAS: the supplier contact and P.I # fill from Odoo only while blank, and what you type is kept.

IPAS: Purchase Order, Received in Odoo (with Partly received) and Create Bill are stamped from Odoo and marked as such. A PO cancelled in Odoo shows a banner and leaves the IPAS open, and a mismatch between Odoo's S numbers and the IPAS's SORs warns.

title: IPAS: raise and track an IPAS from an Odoo purchase order
changes: IPAS: Purchasing can raise an IPAS from an Odoo PO number. The ERP checks the PO in Odoo, gives it a TGIPAS number, and brings in the supplier, currency and item lines.
IPAS: a Project IPAS names its SORs, suggested from the PO's Source Document and analytic accounts. Inventory, Supplies and Events name none.

IPAS: the new IPAS page in the Purchasing menu lists every IPAS by open, filed or cancelled, and by entity and purpose. Purchasing can change the purpose and SORs, or cancel with a reason. The number is kept.
Employees: a new Finance access switch sits beside Purchasing, for Finance staff who read every IPAS.

title: Simpler Offset Request Form
changes: Leaves & Overtime: the Offset tab is now titled "Request Offset", the date field is labelled "Offset Date", and you no longer need to pick a category when requesting an offset.

title: UI Refresh: Responsive queues, cleaner navigation and pagination
changes: Navigation: tabs scroll smoothly with edge indicators on small screens, and the sidebar collapses to a rail on tablets.
Queues and lists: phone-friendly table layouts, shared page numbering across registers and queues, and clearer empty states.
Forms and editing: unsaved edits on Profile and FAQ Editor are protected when navigating away, and sign-in highlights invalid fields inline.
Approvals: declining a leave request now opens the details sheet to add a reason before confirming.

title: Task fixes: Submit for Review and grade colours
changes: Tasks: phased checklists (like Checking and Validation, Release with Payslip) no longer lock Submit for Review, Resubmit or Approve when every item is already ticked.
Tasks: the selected grade (1 to 5) keeps its colour when you hover it instead of turning grey.

title: Purchase Request fixes: stock, chat and who can add items
changes: Purchase Requests: items you've already added now show their stock and when it was checked, so you don't have to look it up in Odoo. Stock checked more than a day ago is marked Stale. New products show no stock.
Purchase Requests: once a request has a Buyer, chat messages notify only the Buyer and the people who asked for items. @mentions still notify the person you mention.

Purchase Requests: the SOR's Deal Team can always add items. The "who can request items" setting on a Stage Action now only adds more people; it no longer locks the Deal Team out. The Flow Canvas wording says so.
Behind the scenes: tidier Purchase Request internals and extra checks. Nothing else changes for you.

title: Keyboard access, clearer errors and tidier wording
changes: Everywhere: rows, cards, filter pills and settings toggles can now be used with the keyboard. Tab to one and press Enter or Space.
Everywhere: if a list fails to load you now see a message with a Retry button instead of an empty page.
Registers and approvals: when your search or filters hide everything, the page says so and offers Clear filters.
Pages: an unknown address now shows a Page not found screen, old links keep their filters, and each page has its own browser tab title.
SORs: the register now scrolls sideways on small screens instead of squashing its columns. Several other small layout fixes on Profile and Offsets.
Wording: clearer success and error messages, correct plurals, and proper … and ’ characters. Empty cells show — and dates look the same everywhere.
Buttons: Approve, Decline and similar buttons can no longer be double-clicked into running twice.

title: Consolidated Purchase Request Item Status
changes: Purchase Requests: Requested item status and action controls are now consolidated into a single interactive status pill with responsive color feedback, removing the redundant Status button and saving space.
Purchase Requests: Polished SlideOver layout, member chip presentation, section spacing, item notes styling, and unified status pill metrics according to design guidelines.
Purchase Requests: Added an Expand / Full Screen button to the SlideOver and redesigned the Purchase Request modal into a responsive two-column split layout with dedicated full-height Chat.

title: Purchase Requests Replace Procurement Requests
changes: Sales Flows: a new Stage Action, Open Purchase Request, opens the SOR's Purchase Request when the SOR enters the Stage, or once a Decider picks Create. An SOR has one request; a second action on a later Stage adds to it.
Sales Flows: everyone with Purchasing access and the SOR's Deal Team become members. On the action you can name a default Buyer, add people or groups, and leave out Deal Team roles.
SORs: purchasing members can open the SOR for the Stage the request was opened on, for as long as the action's access window allows. Other members see the SOR's name and current Stage.
Purchase Requests: each request has its own chat with @mentions and attachments. The Deal Team and the Buyer add items from the SOR's Product List, or request something that isn't in Odoo.

Purchase Requests: Purchasing moves each item along (To order, Canvassing, Ordered, Received, From stock) or closes it. The Buyer can offer a substitute. Ordered items can carry an Odoo PO number, checked against Odoo.
Purchasing: the old Purchasing page is now the Procurement Queue. Take an unassigned request to become its Buyer. A new request with no Buyer notifies Purchasing once.
SORs: the Now, Products and History tabs show the SOR's Purchase Request and its items. A new Stage condition, Purchasing settled, stops an SOR leaving a Stage until every item is closed.
Old procurement requests moved into each SOR's Purchase Request and can no longer be edited. The SOR's old Purchasing panel is gone.

Purchase Requests: when an SOR is deleted or lost while items are still open, the Buyer and the people who asked for items are told, and told again if it comes back. With no Buyer, everyone with Purchasing access hears.
Purchase Requests: the Procurement Queue marks a request whose SOR was deleted or lost, and shows the SOR number when there's no Sales Reference.

Purchasing: someone given Purchasing access joins the requests still being worked. When the access is removed they leave the requests they were only on to buy, and any they were the Buyer of go back to the queue.
Purchase Requests: the chat says who was added or removed, and dialogs opened from a request on an SOR now show in front of it.

Sales Flows: each Terminal Stage now says whether deals end there as Won or Lost. A deal at a Closed Won Stage counts as Won (Realized) instead of lost. Stages named Closed Won were set to Won automatically; set any other winning end Stage to Won in Flow Canvas.

title: Retail Shows Your Real Income, Kept Current
changes: Retail: orders now show the Marketplace Order ID, the marketplace fee and the Order Income typed in the order's Income Note in Odoo.
Retail: the Shopee-versus-Lazada breakdown shows income, orders, average, fees and fee rate for each marketplace.
Retail: the screen now refreshes itself. Orders sync from Odoo every 5 minutes, a nightly run re-reads late notes, and a new order appears on an open Retail screen highlighted.

title: Clearer Change Notes on SORs
changes: SORs: in Activity & Log Notes, changes to a SOR now show as neat labels (old value → new value). Added, removed, changed and renamed products are grouped, and you can open each group to see the details.
SORs: long status labels in the register no longer spill past the table edge. Hover to see the full status.

title: Talk Back and Forth on a Bug Report
changes: Bug reports: IT can now write notes on a report, like 'Fixed, can you check?', and you can reply. Each note notifies the other side.
Bug reports: press the bug button and choose My reports to see the bugs you reported and IT's notes on them.
Bug reports: IT ticks a report Resolved once you confirm the fix, and you see when it was resolved.

title: Faster Pictures
changes: Everywhere: profile pictures and image previews now load a small copy instead of the full photo, so lists, chats and tasks open faster. Clicking a picture still opens it in full.

title: Report a Bug from Any Page
changes: Bug reports: press the bug button at the bottom right of any page, describe what went wrong and add screenshots, videos or any file (paste a screenshot straight in). The IT Team gets it with the page you were on.
Bug reports: IT Team members and Super Admins see every report under Administration → Bug Reports, and tick each one Resolved. Files are deleted a year after a report is sent.
HR: Bug Reports is a new switch under System Access Rights in the employee form. It is on by default for the IT Team.

title: A Big Update: See Everything in Release Notes
changes: Release Notes: a new page under Workspace that shows every change since early September, screen by screen.
SORs: a cleaner register, a Summary when you open an SOR, Revert and Resume, and a Board you can drag SORs across.
Leaves: one form for leave, overtime and the new undertime. Your department head approves first, then HR, and approved requests print with signatures and a QR code.
Approvals: one table each, and you review and decide in a panel at the side.
Retail is now a sales report, and the Commission Dashboard is redesigned.
Everywhere: every page shares one layout, so once you know one, you know them all.

title: Commission Formula in One Place, Tidier Settings
changes: Commission: rates, department allocations and splits are now all on the Formula tab of the Commission Dashboard. The old Commission Pool page in Administration is gone and its link now opens the Formula tab.
Commission: Super Admins can add a new dated rate and edit allocations and positions right on the Formula tab. Sales Directors edit splits. Everyone else can view them.
Settings, Profile and HR Management: setup screens now share the same layout, with underlined tabs and simpler section headings. Profile's Save settings button is now at the top of the page.

title: Retail Is Now a Sales Report
changes: Retail: the screen is now a report. See total sales, number of orders, the average order and this month against last month, with a monthly chart for Shopee and Lazada.
Retail: pick a range (30 days, 3 months, this year, all time or your own dates). Only confirmed orders count, so quotations and cancelled orders are left out of every total.
Retail: orders now come straight from Odoo, so there is nothing to approve. The approval list is hidden for now.

title: Retail Access for Sales
changes: Retail: every Sales employee can now open the Retail screen to review marketplace orders (Shopee, Lazada) and see the totals.
HR: Retail is a new switch under System Access Rights in the employee form. It is on by default for Sales and can be turned off or on for anyone.

title: SORs Redesigned, Revert & Resume, and Group Task Templates
changes: SORs: opening an SOR now shows a two-column Summary first. Open This stage, History and the other views from there.
SORs: new Revert to last stage takes an SOR back one step. When it returns to a stage it was on before, choose Resume previous work or Start fresh.
SORs: the History shows everything done at each stage, including who did it, and loads much faster.
SORs: new My SORs screen lists every SOR you were called into by a task, assignment or purchase request.
SORs: the header is one row, Register is a floating button, and Open and Won totals follow each Sales Flow's own stages.
SORs: fixed the Product List and Estimated Value sometimes doubling.
Sales Flows: the Government and Outright flows are now live.
Group Tasks: tasks have a Start Date and Lead Time, and removing a member now really removes them. Templates brought over are marked (staging) so you can check and adjust them.
Settings: now split into tabs, with leave categories under HR & Schedule. Saved task filters remember every filter.
HR: offset leave can be approved with fewer hours than requested.
Everywhere: fields, tables and pop-ups look and behave the same on every screen.
Updates: when a new version is out, a small notice offers Later or Reload.

title: SOR History Shows Each Stage's Full Work
changes: Opening a stage in the SOR History now shows everything done there, in order: conditions, files, stage fields, stage actions, other tasks, follow-ups and requested items. It also says who gave a file, who ticked a box or who was assigned.
Each stage action shows what it did, including when its task was later deleted or when its decision is being held for a Resume.
Tasks that are on hold or were closed off by Start fresh or a Revert now open read-only, with a note saying when they were held or why they were cancelled.
Tasks closed off by a Revert now show as Cancelled everywhere instead of disappearing, and the stage is marked "Closed off" with who did it and when.
A stage whose work was resumed later is marked "Resumed" instead of showing its old work as unmet.
The History tab loads much faster.

title: Group Tasks: Start Date, Lead Time, and Removing Members
changes: Group tasks now have a Start Date and a Lead Time. Lead Time is a free note, like "120 calendar days" or "Extended". Set them when you create the task, or edit them later from the task's details.

Fixed a bug where removing a member from a group task said it worked, and showed it in the history, but the member stayed on the task. Removing a member now really removes them. If you're not allowed to remove them, it tells you instead.

title: Flow Canvas and Stage History Fixes
changes: Flow Canvas now names the actual person on a Decider card instead of always saying "the assignee" when someone else decides.
Resuming previous work on a returned SOR now correctly carries an already-uploaded condition file forward, so it still counts.
Fixed a rare timing issue where checking off a condition right as a stage move was reverted could get recorded against the wrong stage visit.

title: Rich Deliverables and Group Tasks in SOR History
changes: The SOR History tab now shows actual files and deliverables uploaded during each stage, including document type icons, file sizes, and quick Open buttons.
Group Tasks in stage history are now interactive Task cards: click to open the full Group Task modal, and expand in-place to view members, subtask assignments, and completion status.
Files attached to satisfied conditions are shown directly alongside the checklist items.

title: Revert to Last Stage, Resume or Start Fresh
changes: New "Revert to last stage" on an SOR takes it back to the stage its last move came from, even with no path drawn back and even from Closed Lost. It's available to whoever made the move, the Deal Owner, or a Super Admin, and goes back one step only.

If no work was done on the stage being left, Revert simply undoes the move. If work was done, you choose Keep progress (it's saved for when the SOR comes back) or Remove progress (it's closed off but stays on the SOR's history).
Reverting out of the Won stage clears the Contract Date that move set, and anyone the move notified is told to disregard it.
Moving an SOR back to a stage it has been on before now asks: Resume previous work, or Start fresh.
Tasks from a stage the SOR has left go on hold and drop off everyone's list until the SOR returns. Operations can mark a Stage Action to carry on past its stage instead.

title: SOR Layout Preview (Staging)
changes: Staging only: open any SOR and use the Layout preview bar at the bottom of the window to try different layouts for the SOR window.
Pick one from the menu, use the arrows, or press Shift + Left/Right. Your pick is remembered for every SOR you open.
Nothing about how an SOR works changes; this is for comparing layouts before one is chosen.

title: Settings in Tabs & Saved Task Filters
changes: Settings is now split into tabs: General, Approval Rules, HR & Schedule, Sales Configuration, Employee Groups and System Announcements. You only see the tabs you can use.
Leave categories are now managed in Settings, under HR & Schedule. HR Management has a card that takes you there.
Changing an approval rule in Settings now takes effect in open approval queues straight away, with no page reload.
On Tasks, "Save filters as default" now remembers every filter, not just SORS.
On Tasks and Group Tasks, the save button now shows "Default saved" once saved, or "Update default" if you have changed the filters since.
The Commission Pool card in Settings can now be opened with the keyboard.

title: Fixed: SOR Product List Could Double
changes: Fixed a bug where an SOR's Product List, and its Estimated Value, could double when the SOR was open in more than one place at the same time.
Opening an SOR no longer adds a false "Added product(s)" entry to its timeline.

title: One-Row SORS Header & Floating Register Button
changes: The SORS header is now a single row: search and results on the left, view tabs and Filters on the right, so switching views no longer moves them.
Search and the SOR count, Open and Won figures appear on List and Board only. Figures are shortened (e.g. ₱353.7M); hover for the exact amount.
The Filters button shows how many filters are on. On Overview and Deleted it stays in place, greyed out.
Register is now a floating button at the bottom-right, clear of the environment banner.
On phones, the view tabs and Filters show icons only.

title: One Consistent Look for Fields, Tables and Pop-ups
changes: Dropdown pickers, form fields, tables, pop-up windows and side panels now look and behave the same on every screen, so the app feels like one product instead of a mix of one-off designs.
Pick-lists that used the browser's plain dropdown (filters, page size, employee and offset forms) now use the app's own dropdown, with keyboard support, and still work inside the Filters menu.
Pop-up windows, the notifications panel and the mobile menu now open and close smoothly, and close the same way everywhere: press Escape or click outside.
Tables in SORS, Purchasing, HR, Offsets and Group Tasks share one look, and the login and reset-password buttons now match the rest of the app.

title: Unified All SORs Filter & Cleaner Filters Menu
changes: Added an 'All SORs' option across SORS view filters and the Kanban Board flow switcher.
The Filters popover now features a clean, well-spaced 4-row layout with aligned dropdowns and quick toggles, making filtering fast and easy to navigate.
Selecting 'All SORs' on the Kanban Board presents a clear guide and quick-select buttons for each Sales Flow, or a one-click switch to the List view.

title: Stage Conditions & Fields Inline Editing & Live Preview
changes: Editing a condition or field in a Stage now opens the editor directly below the item rather than jumping to the top of the panel, making editing feel seamless and in-context.
The Fields tab now includes a live preview matching how the field and its input look on the SOR, giving an immediate look at required badges, help text, and selection options.

title: Dynamic Open Pipeline & Won Calculation
changes: The Open pipeline and Won totals in SORS now follow each Sales Flow's actual stages dynamically from the Flow Canvas.

An SOR is counted under Open pipeline while it is moving through stages before the Won stage. Once it reaches the Won stage or continues to post-award fulfillment stages (like Delivery or Invoicing), it counts toward Won.
Deals that are closed lost or cancelled are excluded from both totals, ensuring the pipeline accurately reflects active work.

title: My SORs
changes: Sales > My SORs is a new screen listing every SOR you were called into by a task, an assignment, or a purchase request. Until now those SORs appeared nowhere: the SORS register only lists SORs you own or are named on, so being called in gave you access with no way to find the record again except the notification.
Each row says which Stage called you in and how far your access reaches, in the same words the Flow Canvas uses for that setting. Opening one shows the same view the notification opens.
SORs whose access has since closed stay on the screen under Closed, so work you did last month is still findable.
The sidebar entry carries a count of the SORs you currently have open access to, and is visible to everyone — anyone can be called into an SOR, including people with no Sales access.

title: Approve Offset Leave With Edited Hours
changes: When HR approves offset leave, they can now change the number of hours before approving. It starts at the hours requested and can't go higher.
Where the approved hours differ from the hours requested, the leave lists show both: the requested hours crossed out, next to the hours approved.

title: CRM Is Called SORS
changes: The CRM module is now called SORS — the Sales Opportunity Registration System, the name it has in company policy (CCPR-2026-001, Annex C). One SOR is one Sales Opportunity Registration.

Its address changed from /crm to /sors, and the Commission Dashboard and Commission Formula moved with it. Old links still work: anything pointing at /crm or /opportunities, including links inside notifications you have not opened yet, lands in the right place.
The filter on Tasks and Group Tasks that shows only work linked to an SOR is now labelled SORS.

title: Retail Has Its Own Screen
changes: Retail has moved out of the SOR register and into its own entry in the sidebar, under Sales. The register's tabs are now just List, Board, Overview and Deleted.

The new screen shows marketplace orders waiting for review at the top, and what has already been counted — totals by month and storefront — below. Orders only appear at the top when there is something to review.
Who can open it has not changed: Super Admins and Sales Directors, the same as before the move.

title: A Tidier SOR Window
changes: The SOR window now has tabs. It opens on Now, which shows what the current Stage needs today: what's blocking it first, then the Stage's fields, any decisions waiting on you, the tasks, and the next follow-up.
Each task is now one line with its people, how many parts are done and its due date. Click the arrow on a group task to see each person's part, or click the title to open the task.
Journey lists every Stage the SOR has been through, newest first, with what was done on each.
Items holds the Product List with search and stock levels. Its header stays in place as you scroll long lists. If the list is empty, it tells you to fetch from Odoo or to add a Sales Reference first.
Details holds the SOR's fields, the Deal Team, Estimated Value, the quotation buttons, commission, and Inclusions and Purchasing.

title: Reusable Employee Groups
changes: Super Admins can now set up Employee Groups in Settings: named sets of people made of hand-picked employees and whole teams, so later Sales Flow settings can say who they are about once and reuse it.
A group always means its current members. When someone joins or leaves a team, every group that includes that team follows automatically.

title: Safer Stage Checklist & Accurate Pipeline
changes: Saving a field from a Stage Checklist now changes only that field. The rest of the SOR, including the Deal Team, dates and Product List, stays as it was.
After you move an SOR, the tasks the move created and the new Stage's checklist show right away, without reopening the SOR. If an automation fails, you're told which one so you can create it by hand.
Tasks created for an SOR now link back to it from both the task and Group Task windows.
Open pipeline value now leaves out won and lost SORs, and the Open filter lists exactly the SORs it adds up.

title: Clearer Flow Modes & Accurate Draft Diffing
changes: Renamed the misleading 'Restore into draft' button to 'Revert to this version', with clear confirmation explaining that your draft will take on that version's rules without altering live deals until you publish.
The Draft version row in the left-hand Versions panel is now directly clickable to return to draft mode at any time, with clear selection highlighting and an 'Editing' status badge.

The top version-preview banner is now reassuring and friendly for new users: featuring a clear 'Back to draft' action with back arrow, an explicit (X) close button, and a separate, guarded 'Revert to this version' action with helpful tooltip explanations.

Fixed false diff changes: stages are no longer reported as changed when nothing changed. The comparator now compares actual process properties (name, sequence, terminal status, brackets, colors) rather than database timestamps, coordinates, or PostgreSQL key ordering.
Clicking 'Compare with draft' in the version rail now automatically expands the version and reveals the exact comparison against your unpublished changes with a single click.
Canvas editing is now strictly locked when viewing a published flow: stages and moves cannot be moved or deleted until you click 'Edit draft', eliminating confusion between live and draft states.
Prominent status badges make your current mode obvious at a glance: 'Live' on published versions, 'Editing' when modifying a draft, and 'Viewing' when inspecting version history.
Expanded the Versions panel with generous padding, comfortable spacing between version cards, and improved readability for version notes, author stamps, and comparisons.

title: Cleaner Flow Canvas Layout & Intuitive Popovers
changes: The Flow Canvas controls are now cleanly anchored across the screen: the Sale Type switcher aligns with the version history rail on the left, while status indicators and publish actions sit neatly on the right.
Canvas navigation tools (minimap and zoom controls) are logically grouped in the bottom-right corner, and the Add Stage button is a clear, polished action in the bottom-left.
Menus and popovers — including unpublished changes and the Add Stage dialog — now reliably close whenever you click away on the canvas or press the Escape key.

title: Roomier Flow Publish Window
changes: The publish dialog on the Sales Flow canvas is now wider and more spacious, with increased padding and comfortable room for reviewing draft changes.
Long change lists now scroll neatly inside the window, keeping the Cancel and Publish action buttons always visible and accessible.

title: Publish vX.Y
changes: "Lock this flow" is now "Publish", and it shows the version number the click will create — "Publish v3.2" — straight from the database, so the preview and the result can never disagree. "Unlock" is now "Edit draft" and still asks for a reason.

Versions now carry meaning: v3.2 tells you it's a routine refinement of v3.x, while v4.0 means a Stage was removed or the Won Stage changed and deals on the old version may not move up safely. Adding, renaming or rewiring Stages is minor; losing a Stage or changing the Won Stage starts a new major version.
A Sales Flow's first publish is v1.0. Every version already on record — v1, v2, v3 — now reads as v1.0, v2.0, v3.0, so the numbers on old deals still match their history notes.
The version badge on an SOR, the version page, the history dialog and a deal's own history notes all read vX.Y now.

title: See a Past Version's Stage Rules
changes: On the read-only Sales Flow version page you reach from an SOR's version badge, clicking a Stage now opens its panel and shows that version's actual Stage Conditions and Stage Actions — read from the saved version itself, not from the flow as it stands today. Until now the page showed only counts.
The panel has no editing controls; the live flow is still edited only on the Flow Canvas.
A version that was locked before any Conditions or Actions were drawn now says so plainly instead of showing an empty panel.

title: Flow Canvas Is One Canvas Now
changes: The Flow Canvas no longer has a Live/Sandbox switch. It opens straight onto the real Sales Flow, which is the only thing it ever edited that mattered — the shared Sandbox scratch space has been retired.
You still see who else is working on the same flow, and a Super Admin can still open the Snapshot History from the canvas.

title: Password Reset Links That Hold Up
changes: Password reset links no longer stop working before you get to them. Some email systems quietly open every link in a message to check it's safe, which used to use up your one-time reset link — so clicking it yourself gave an error. The link is now only spent when you actually open it.

The reset page tells you where you stand instead of guessing: it shows a brief check while your link is verified, opens the password form only once the link is confirmed good, and says plainly when a link has expired or has already been used — with a way straight back to the login page.
Saving a new password no longer fails with a confusing "session missing" message.
Having the portal open in another tab no longer interrupts a reset you're in the middle of.
Opening the reset page without a link from an email now says so, instead of showing a password form that couldn't work. To change a password you already know, use your profile.

title: Desktop Notifications
changes: You can now turn on Desktop Notifications from Settings, so a mention, a task assigned to you, a decision on your request, or an approval waiting on you can reach you even with the portal closed.
Turn it off again anytime from the same toggle — it only ever asks for permission after you turn it on.
Everything still shows up in the notification drawer as before; desktop notifications are in addition to that, not a replacement.
Deleting a notification now actually removes it, instead of coming back on your next visit.

title: A Second Way In: Email + Password Login
changes: Signing in with email and password is now a real, supported route alongside Google — no longer a disabled test form.
New employees are issued a password when their account is created; a banner reminds you while you're still on it, and it dismisses without blocking anything.
Change your password anytime from your profile, or reset it from the login page if you've forgotten it — both go through an emailed verification link.
A Super Admin can reissue a lost first-day password from Employee Management, but only while the employee hasn't yet set their own — after that, it's email verification only.

title: Undertime Requests, Filing Through Printing
changes: You can now file for Undertime alongside Overtime, Offset, and SIL from the same Apply modal — record the scheduled work window, the window actually worked, and a purpose; the shortfall between the two is computed for you.
The scheduled window pre-fills from your department's working-week schedule for the day you pick, but stays fully editable.

Undertime goes through the same department-head approval stage as every other request type before HR makes the final call, with an editable approved-hours field on HR's side — no paid/offset choice, since undertime never touches your offset or SIL balance.
Employee Balances now shows a derived 'Undertime (this month)' column — summed from approved requests only, never a stored balance.
Approved undertime prints as its own TG-13 form, with the same QR verification and signature plates (Employee, Department Head, HR) as Overtime and Leave forms.

title: Department Head Approval for Leaves & Overtime
changes: SIL leave, offset leave, and overtime requests now go to your department head for approval first, before HR makes the final decision.
When you apply, the system automatically fills in your department head based on your department and sub-department. If it can't tell for sure who that is, you'll be asked to pick one yourself.
Department heads approve or reject requests with their own e-signature, and you'll get a notification as soon as they decide.
If a department head isn't available, HR can override the head-approval step and proceed directly, with the reason recorded for the record.

title: Deal Visibility Now Enforced by the Server
changes: Sales Opportunity Records are now only visible to the people actually attached to a deal (registrar, owner, supporting salespeople, sales director), plus department heads, HR, and Super Admins — a stray API call can no longer reveal every deal in the company.
Tasks and Group Tasks now carry real database-level access rules matching what the screens already showed, closing a gap where those tables previously accepted reads and writes from anyone.
A salesperson with no visible deals now sees a clear empty state instead of anything that could look broken.

title: See the Exact Flow Version Your Deal Is On
changes: Each deal in the SOR now shows a version badge (e.g. 'Government · v1') next to the stage control, so you can tell at a glance which set of rules that deal is following.
Click the badge to open a read-only canvas of that version — centred on the deal's current stage so you immediately see where you are and what comes next.
Deals pin to a flow version at registration and stay there for life. If the flow has since been updated, the badge is what tells the truth about which rules actually apply.

title: Grouped Checklists with Smart Progressive Disclosure
changes: Organize long checklists into distinct sections and phases with an inline '+ Add Section' button.
Smart Progressive Disclosure: Completed phases automatically collapse into clean summary bars so you can focus on the active phase without visual clutter.
Visual Step Indicators: Kanban cards and table views now show active step progress (e.g. Step 2 of 3) alongside total item counts.
100% Backward Compatible: Simple, un-sectioned checklists continue to look and work exactly as before with zero disruption.

title: Flow Canvas Collaborative Editing & Realtime Preview
changes: Enabled real-time live preview in Flow Canvas: see who else is viewing the canvas with active user indicators, live collaborative cursors, and real-time node drag previews across both Live and Sandbox modes.
Opened Flow Canvas editing to all authenticated team members so everyone can collaborate on sales flows, stages, conditions, and actions.
Fixed an issue where switching to Sandbox mode did not properly activate collaborative presence and shared document editing.

title: Retail Orders Queue
changes: Added a new 'Retail Queue' tab in the SOR/CRM module where Shopee retail orders from Odoo are held for review before entering the Sales Opportunity Register.
Sales users can now review each queued order, edit the details (client name, buyer, amount, deal owner), and approve with one click to create the official SOR entry.
Dismissed orders are tracked with an audit trail and never appear in the SOR. If the order is still present in Odoo the next sync cycle, it stays dismissed.

title: Automated Odoo to SOR Lead Syncing
changes: Added a background cron job that automatically syncs materialized sales (regular and retail/Shopee) from Odoo directly to the Sales Opportunity Register.
Shopee sales without a prior lead are now automatically created as Closed Won in the SOR, saving sales from manual double-entry.
The background sync also automatically pulls any attached Proofs of Payment straight from the Odoo log and attaches them to the new deal in the SOR.

title: Plan a Flow Together, and Safer Leave Withdrawals
changes: Two people can now open the same Flow Plan and work on it at once — adding, moving, renaming and deleting Stages all appear for everyone straight away, with nobody's work overwriting anyone else's and nobody needing to reload.

You can see who else has a Flow Plan open, with a named cursor for each person. Live cursors have moved off the operational Flow Canvas, which edits the real flow, onto Flow Plans, where working together is the point.
A leave you have already taken can no longer be withdrawn for a refund of its hours. If an approved leave was genuinely never taken, HR can undo the approval to put the hours back.

Approving, undoing or withdrawing an offset or SIL leave now moves every day of a multi-day leave and the hours balance together, so a leave can never end up half-decided and two HR officers acting at the same time can no longer lose a balance change between them.

title: Flow Plan Sandbox & Purchasing Queue Improvements
changes: Introduced a new Flow Plans sandbox where you can draft and experiment with sales flows without affecting production data.
The Purchasing Queue now includes a filter bar, allowing you to instantly filter requests by Assignee, Outcome, and SOR.
You can now quickly reassign a Purchasing request to another employee directly from its row in the queue.
Upgraded the HR and Employee Leaves pages to update instantly when a leave is approved or rejected, eliminating unnecessary full page reloads.

title: Leave Manager Landing Page Fix
changes: Leave managers who navigate directly to /hr are now correctly redirected to Offsets & Leaves, instead of being bounced to the dashboard.

title: Leave Balances Now Account for Pending Requests
changes: Applying for offset or SIL leave now checks your available balance (what's left after your own pending requests), not just your total balance — closing a gap where several pending requests together could add up to more hours than you actually have.
The apply form and the HR pending queue now both show available hours, not the raw balance.
A refused application now tells you how many hours are already committed to pending requests and how many are left.

title: Leave Calendar Privacy Fix
changes: Leave reasons are no longer sent to colleagues' browsers when viewing the shared leave calendar. Only the details needed to render the calendar card (name, date, hours, time window) are loaded for other people's leaves.

title: HR Activity Log Access
changes: HR officers can now open the HR Activity Log from the Human Resources section of the sidebar, instead of needing a Super Admin to open it for them.

title: Leave Manager Redirect Fix
changes: Leave managers who navigate directly to /hr are now correctly redirected to Offsets & Leaves, instead of being bounced to the dashboard.

title: HR Config Screen Robustness
changes: Printed form settings now work even on a database with no settings row yet — saving creates it instead of erroring.
The activity log search no longer sends a request on every keystroke.
Config screens no longer throw if they render before your session finishes loading.
Deactivating a leave category now asks for confirmation, matching Delete elsewhere in the module.

title: HR Leave Categories Reliability
changes: Reordering leave categories is now processed as a single atomic operation, preventing partial saves when reordering long lists.
Adding a new category is now safe against concurrent modifications by multiple HR admins.

title: HR Module Consistency & Polish
changes: The Leaves Manager page now shows one title instead of two stacked headers.
The page, navigation, and tab now all use the same name for this screen.
Loading states across the HR module now consistently show a spinner instead of bare text.
The Employees and Categories tabs now share the same card style.
Deleting an employee now uses the same styled confirmation prompt as other destructive actions, replacing the plain browser dialog.

title: HR Module Visual Improvements
changes: Removed hardcoded colors across the HR module to ensure it displays correctly in dark mode.
Replaced several flat palette steps with theme tokens for a more consistent visual hierarchy.

title: Fixed HR Verification Queue Filtering
changes: Super admins are now properly filtered out of the HR Verification employee filter.
Backlog staleness is now accurately measured based on when a task was graded, rather than when it was originally logged.

title: HR Verification Load Optimization
changes: Fixed an issue where non-HR users visiting the HR Verification route would trigger unnecessary data loading before being redirected.
Optimized the HR Verification page to reuse cached employee and category lists, significantly improving load times.

title: Undo Now Works After Bulk Actions
changes: The Undo button that appears after bulk-verifying, approving, or declining tasks now actually works â€” previously it was silently ignored due to a library incompatibility.

title: Consistent Leave Rules for Offset and SIL
changes: Applying for SIL leave on a Saturday or Sunday is now blocked, matching Offset leave.

The 1-hour lunch deduction on a leave window of 5+ hours now applies consistently to Offset and SIL, single-day and date-range applications, and the amount shown in the form now matches what gets recorded.
Only Regular employees can file for or be approved for SIL leave, closing a gap where a Probationary or OJT employee could spend a SIL balance they were not entitled to.

title: Employee Directory Improvements
changes: Added new filters for Employment Status and Leave Manager in the Employee Directory.
Improved the reliability of employee email duplication checks.
Fixed an issue where the +40 SIL auto-grant was not reflected in the balance input field before saving.
Improved the Self-Service Leaves page to group multi-day leaves into a single application row for easier viewing.

title: HR Overtime Fix & Audit Trail Updates
changes: Fixed an issue where deactivated employees were still visible in the Employee Balances register and HR file-for-employee picker.
Completed the HR audit trail to now track when leave categories are renamed, reordered, or deactivated, and when form printed settings are changed.
Fixed an issue where the Document Center print tray would lose its staged records if the page was reloaded or the month was changed.
Fixed an issue where HR officers were unable to file overtime on behalf of employees.

title: Group Task Mentions, Stage Requirement Notices & Odoo Inclusions Import
changes: Fixed group task mentions (@name) so every employee can see and tag the full team, not just managers.
Adding a new requirement to a Sales Flow stage now leaves a note on the timeline of every deal already sitting there, explaining what changed.
SOR Inclusions can now be imported directly from the linked Odoo quotation, ready to review and edit before saving.

title: Sales Flow Lock & Condition Improvements
changes: Sales Flows can now be locked and unlocked directly from the Flow Canvas, with a clear list of what's blocking a lock.
Adding a 'Field on record' condition to a Stage now lets you specify which field to check.
Fixed a bug in the Purchasing request form where quickly typing a buyer's name right after opening the form could scramble the product name field.

title: Changelog Feature Introduced
changes: Added a new 'What's Changed' modal to announce updates natively within the application.
Established standard practice for recording version control updates.
